title: Gethsemane — the cup in the Father's hand, and not as I will, but as thou wilt (Psalm 75; Isaiah 51; John 10; Hebrews 5; Zechariah 13)
summary:
It ain't new. The cup he prayed over in the garden was already in the Father's hand in the Psalms and the prophets, and the prayer itself, not my will but thine, is what the Son had said of himself all along. Matthew sets the scene:

*Then cometh Yahusha (Jesus) with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and saith unto the disciples, Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder.* (Matthew 26:36)

*Then saith he unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry ye here, and watch with me.* (Matthew 26:38)

*And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.* (Matthew 26:39)

The soul cast down was the psalmist's before it was his:

*Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in Elohim (God): for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance.* (Psalm 42:5)

And the cup is not a figure Matthew made up. It is the cup of fury in the hand of Yahuah (LORD), poured out and drunk to the dregs:

*For in the hand of Yahuah (LORD) there is a cup, and the wine is red; it is full of mixture; and he poureth out of the same: but the dregs thereof, all the wicked of the earth shall wring them out, and drink them.* (Psalm 75:8)

*Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand of Yahuah (LORD) the cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out.* (Isaiah 51:17)

*Thus saith thy Yahuah (Lord) Yahuah (LORD), and thy Elohim (God) that pleadeth the cause of his people, Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling, even the dregs of the cup of my fury; thou shalt no more drink it again:* (Isaiah 51:22)

Isaiah says the cup is taken out of Jerusalem's hand. In the garden it is put into his. He had already asked the sons of Zebedee whether they could drink it:

*But Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.* (Matthew 20:22)

Luke adds the angel and the sweat:

*Saying, Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.* (Luke 22:42)

*And there appeared an angel unto him from heaven, strengthening him.* (Luke 22:43)

*And being in an agony he prayed more earnestly: and his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground.* (Luke 22:44)

Read what the prayer is. It is the Son asking the Father, and the Son's will bending to the Father's will. He is Elohim (God), and he has a Father, and he does the Father's will. He said so before the garden, said it in the garden, and said it from the cross:

*Then answered Yahusha (Jesus) and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise.* (John 5:19)

*Now is my soul troubled; and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour: but for this cause came I unto this hour.* (John 12:27)

*And when Yahusha (Jesus) had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.* (Luke 23:46)

Nobody took the life from him. The cup was drunk because he chose to drink it, and the choosing was the Father's commandment kept:

*No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment have I received of my Father.* (John 10:18)

Hebrews says plainly what the garden was:

*Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared;* (Hebrews 5:7)

*Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;* (Hebrews 5:8)

And Paul says that same mind is the one we are to carry:

*Let this mind be in you, which was also in HaMashiach Yahusha (Christ Jesus):* (Philippians 2:5)

*And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.* (Philippians 2:8)

Set Abraham beside it. He also rose early and went up the mountain with his only son, and Matthew does not say the word; put the two side by side and read:

*And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.* (Genesis 22:2)

Then the hour comes, the shepherd is struck as Zechariah said, and the sheep run:

*Then cometh he to his disciples, and saith unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of Adam is betrayed into the hands of sinners.* (Matthew 26:45)

*Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones.* (Zechariah 13:7)

The sheep who scattered that night are the little ones his hand turns toward. They slept while he prayed, and the charge he gave them in the garden is still the charge:

*Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.* (Matthew 26:41)

3048.prose: Mark sets the same garden and the same words. Yahusha (Jesus) leaves the disciples sitting and goes off to pray, and Mark has him say it just as Matthew does, *Sit ye here*. Two witnesses agree on the place and on what he came there to do.
3048.phrase: he saith to his disciples, Sit ye here, while I shall pray
3048.sentence: Mark names the same place and the same instruction, and says the going apart was for prayer.

3049.prose: Luke tells where Gethsemane sat. It was on the mount of Olives, and he went there *as he was wont*, the way he always did. So the garden was no sudden turning. He walked to his usual place with the disciples following, and there the cup was waiting.
3049.phrase: as he was wont, to the mount of Olives; and his disciples also followed him
3049.sentence: Luke places the garden on the mount of Olives, where he went by habit, with the disciples following behind him.

3050.prose: John gives the garden its ground. Yahusha (Jesus) had finished speaking to his disciples, and he crossed the brook Cedron and went into a garden. Matthew gives only the name Gethsemane. John says it lay over the brook, a real place with a real way to it.
3050.phrase: he went forth with his disciples over the brook Cedron, where was a garden
3050.sentence: John names the garden across the brook Cedron, the same place Matthew calls Gethsemane.

3051.prose: Before Yahusha (Jesus) says his soul is sorrowful, the psalmist asks his own soul why it is *cast down*. It is the same weight on the same soul, and the psalm already has the answer: *hope thou in Elohim (God)*. The soul that is low is told where to look.
3051.phrase: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me
3051.sentence: The psalmist's soul is cast down and told to hope in Elohim (God), the same weight Yahusha (Jesus) carries into the garden.

3052.prose: The psalm says it twice. At its close the cast down soul is asked its question again, and the answer holds: *hope thou in Elohim (God)*. Yahusha (Jesus) goes to a garden to pray with his soul under that same weight, and the psalm has already shown where a soul like that turns.
3052.phrase: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my Elohim (God)
3052.sentence: The refrain comes round again and ends in praise, showing where the troubled soul looks when it is cast down.

3053.prose: A third time the psalmist stops and talks to his own soul. Heavy and low, it is told to hope in Elohim (God) and to praise him yet. That is the road Yahusha (Jesus) takes into the garden. His sorrow goes up to the Father and does not go away from him.
3053.phrase: hope in Elohim (God): for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance
3053.sentence: The refrain returns a third time, again telling the cast down soul to hope in Elohim (God).

3054.prose: Here is the cup, and it is already in a hand. It is in the hand of Yahuah (LORD), red wine full of mixture, poured out, with the dregs for the wicked to drink. When Yahusha (Jesus) goes off to pray, the cup he will name was not made up that night. It was the Father's to pour.
3054.phrase: in the hand of Yahuah (LORD) there is a cup, and the wine is red
3054.sentence: The cup is held in the hand of Yahuah (LORD) long before the garden, red and full of mixture.

3055.prose: Jerusalem drank this cup first. Isaiah tells her to wake and stand up, because she had drunk from the hand of Yahuah (LORD) *the cup of his fury* down to the dregs. This is the cup under the prayer in the garden. Matthew did not make it up; Isaiah had it in the hand of Yahuah (LORD) first.
3055.phrase: which hast drunk at the hand of Yahuah (LORD) the cup of his fury
3055.sentence: Jerusalem has already drunk the cup of fury from the hand of Yahuah (LORD), the same cup Yahusha (Jesus) later prays over.

3056.prose: The cup is taken *out of thine hand*, and Jerusalem is told she will drink it no more. Isaiah says it leaves her hand. In the garden it is Yahusha (Jesus) who takes it up, so the prayer over the cup is a prayer over this very cup.
3056.phrase: I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling, even the dregs of the cup of my fury
3056.sentence: The cup is lifted out of Jerusalem's hand with a promise she will not drink it again, and the garden puts it into his.

3057.prose: The cup passes from a hand again. Yahuah (LORD) tells Jeremiah to *Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand* and carry it out. It is always his cup, and it is given out by him. So the cup Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of in the garden has a long line of hands, and the first hand is the Father's.
3057.phrase: Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations
3057.sentence: The cup of fury is handed out from the hand of Yahuah (LORD) himself, so the cup in the garden is his to give.

3058.prose: John gives the same troubled soul and the same turn. Yahusha (Jesus) asks what he should say, and what he says is *Father, save me from this hour*. Then he names why he is there: *for this cause came I unto this hour*. He does not run. The troubled soul goes to the Father.
3058.phrase: Father, save me from this hour: but for this cause came I unto this hour
3058.sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) says his soul is troubled and asks the Father to save him from the hour, then names it as the reason he came.

3060.prose: Paul points at Yahusha (Jesus) and tells the saints to carry the mind he had. Read beside the garden, that mind is the Son who asks the Father and then bows his own will to the Father's will. It is a low and willing mind, and it holds all the way to the cross.
3060.phrase: Let this mind be in you, which was also in HaMashiach Yahusha (Christ Jesus)
3060.sentence: Paul tells them to have the mind that was in Yahusha (Jesus), the mind that bows to the Father in the garden.

3061.prose: Before the garden he had already named the cup. Two brothers ask for seats, and he asks them, *Are ye able to drink of the cup*? They say *We are able*. They did not know what they asked. The cup was his to drink, and he was walking toward it with his eyes open.
3061.phrase: Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of
3061.sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) already speaks of the cup as his own to drink, and asks if the sons of Zebedee can share it.

3062.prose: Matthew tells at the start that Yahusha (Jesus) was *led up of the Spirit* into the wilderness to be tempted. The garden is another hard place he goes into on purpose. He is brought to both, and in both he does not turn aside. The hour in the garden is not the first time his obedience is tested.
3062.phrase: was Yahusha (Jesus) led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted
3062.sentence: He was led into the wilderness to be tempted, so the testing in the garden is not the first time he is led into a hard place.

3063.prose: He says the Father loves him because he lays down his life. That is the garden said ahead of time. He is not caught and dragged. He gives himself, and he gives himself to the Father, who loves him for it. The cup is drunk by choice, and the choosing is a Son answering his Father.
3063.phrase: doth my Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I might take it again
3063.sentence: The Father's love is tied to the Son laying down his life, which makes the garden a gift given and not a loss taken.

3064.prose: Elohim (God) tests Abraham, and Abraham answers, *Behold, here I am*. The very next word is about taking his son. Set that beside the garden and the two sit together: a father's word, a son going toward it, and an answer that does not argue. Matthew does not say the word. Put the two side by side.
3064.phrase: Elohim (God) did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am
3064.sentence: Elohim (God) tests Abraham and he answers here I am, the start of the offering of his only son that the garden sits beside.

7115.prose: Matthew gives the same prayer in his own words. *O my Father, if it be possible*, let this cup pass, and then the turn, *not as I will, but as thou wilt*. Luke says it a little differently, but it is one prayer. The Son asks the Father, and the Son's will bends to the Father's.
7115.phrase: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt
7115.sentence: Matthew records the same prayer, the cup asked away and the Son's will given over to the Father's.

5319.prose: Mark brings him to a place to pray, and Isaiah shows what weight the prayer carries. Jerusalem had drunk *the cup of his fury* from the hand of Yahuah (LORD) and wrung out the dregs of it. The cup is old and it is real, and it is the Father's.
5319.phrase: thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out
5319.sentence: Jerusalem drank the dregs of the cup of trembling, so the cup he prays over was already a known and heavy thing.

5320.prose: Mark brings him to the place of prayer, and Jeremiah shows whose cup it is. Yahuah (LORD) hands the wine cup of fury to the prophet and sends him to carry it out. The cup is poured from the hand of Yahuah (LORD) and given to whom he chooses. That is the hand the Son looks to when he prays.
5320.phrase: Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations
5320.sentence: The cup of fury is given out from the hand of Yahuah (LORD), so it is his to hand over.

5318.prose: Hebrews says what the garden was. In the days of his flesh he offered prayers *with strong crying and tears* to the one able to save him from death, and he was heard. He asked, he feared, and he was heard. The Son at prayer in Mark's garden is the same Son who prayed this way.
5318.phrase: offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death
5318.sentence: Hebrews names the garden prayer, strong crying and tears to the one able to save him from death, and says he was heard.

5321.prose: He says the spirit is ready and the flesh is weak. Paul says the same weakness in his own words: to will is with him, but to do the good he finds not. The charge to watch and pray stands because the weakness stands. Paul also calls the law good in the same passage, so the weakness is in the flesh and not in the law.
5321.phrase: for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not
5321.sentence: Paul names the same split between willing and doing that Yahusha (Jesus) gives as the reason to watch and pray.

5322.prose: Paul describes the same pull. The flesh wants one way and the Spirit another, and a man cannot do all he would. Yahusha (Jesus) said it to sleeping men in the garden and gave them the way through, *Watch ye and pray*. The weakness is plain, and so is the charge that goes with it.
5322.phrase: the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh
5322.sentence: Paul describes the same pull between flesh and Spirit that Yahusha (Jesus) names when he finds the disciples asleep.

5323.prose: The hour has come and he is handed to sinners, and Isaiah had already said who laid it on him. *All we like sheep have gone astray*, each to his own way, and it was Yahuah (LORD) who laid the weight on him. Judas does the handing, but the hand behind it is Yahuah (LORD).
5323.phrase: Yahuah (LORD) hath laid on him the iniquity of us all
5323.sentence: Isaiah says the laying of the iniquity on him was the work of Yahuah (LORD), behind the betrayal to sinners.

5324.prose: Judas comes with swords and staves, and Zechariah had already heard the order given. Yahuah (LORD) calls the sword against the shepherd, and the sheep are scattered. The crowd with its weapons is the sword the prophet saw. The scattered are *the little ones* his hand turns toward.
5324.phrase: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones
5324.sentence: Zechariah has the shepherd struck and the sheep scattered, and the hand that strikes then turns toward the little ones.

5352.prose: Mark gives only the loud cry and the giving up of the ghost. Luke tells what the cry was: *Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit*. The last thing he does is what he did in the garden. He gives himself over to the Father.
5352.phrase: Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost
5352.sentence: Luke gives the words of the loud cry, the spirit handed into the Father's hands.

5351.prose: He gave up the ghost, and John says no one took it from him. *I lay it down of myself*, he says, and he had the power to take it up again. It was a commandment from his Father. So the loud cry is a Son keeping a charge, not a man overpowered.
5351.phrase: No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself
5351.sentence: No one takes the life from him. He lays it down by the Father's commandment, so the death is the Son's own act of obedience.

fable_read: Claude Fable 5.1 read every card: 3055 'no picture, a real cup' reworded (the cup is Isaiah's figure, not denied); 3056 'someone has to hold it in her place' removed (Isaiah 51:23 sends it to her afflicters; the summary says only that it leaves her hand and is put into his); 3064 'laid side by side to be read' tightened. 5352 reworded: a 9-word run of Mark 15:37 outside italics.
